summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,568.92 on Nov 3. That is about 3.2% below its Oct 6 record and below a flattening 50-day average (~7,697), but still above the rising 200-day (~7,313). Futures are down 1.1–1.3% this morning (Nasdaq-100 about -2%) as a Democratic midterm sweep raises the risk of AI and data-center regulation. Breadth is holding up (~61% of members above their 50-day) as rotation into equal-weight continues, but VIX is ~21 and rising, and HY spreads have widened to ~340bp from ~270bp in late August. On Oct 28 the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% with two hawkish dissents. Q3 GDP of 3.4% and core PCE of 3.1% y/y, plus Logan and Musalem calling for more hikes, keep a Dec 9 hike about 85% priced, so the Nov 10 CPI print is the key test. Add new cash only after CPI, favor equal-weight and non-AI names over crowded mega-cap tech, and treat ~7,300 (the 200-day) as the line that would flip this to WAIT.
